_doc: Controlled --wal-fsync-parallel (checkpoint per-stream fdatasync fan-out) ladder at the winning shard count (4), on the SAME NVMe cluster as wal-shard-sweep (cluster_name bench-walshard, idempotent reuse). The shard sweep showed throughput is device-flush-bound and shard-insensitive (~72-75k); the remaining question is whether parallelizing the checkpoint's O(N_touched) per-stream fdatasync storm (which competes with commit fsyncs for the device flush budget) helps or hurts. Prior data only had fanout 1 vs 16 (16 regressed); this sweeps 1/2/4/8 to properly characterize whether a SMALL fanout helps before device contention dominates. Same 200k streams / 8 vCPU pin / 256 conns so it's directly comparable to wal-s4.
